title: Onomasticon Genre Pack
description: A genre pack declares how names get generated for a slice of the naming space (a culture, a setting, a sub-genre). Genre is data, not code: adding a new one is authoring a pack file, not writing a strategy.

schemaVersion.description: Bump only on breaking changes to this schema; lets the loader reject or migrate packs it can't read.

id.description: Dotted namespace, e.g. 'highfantasy.elven'. Must be unique across all loaded packs.

label.description: Human-readable name shown in the picker UI.

packVersion.description: The pack content's own version (semver-ish), independent of schemaVersion. Bump when entries/formats change.

tags.description: Free-form facets for filtering in the UI, e.g. ['fantasy','elven']. Not used in matching logic.

strategy.description: Which generation strategy this pack's config targets. 'template' ships in v1; third-party strategies register their own id and config shape via the strategy registry.

lexiconRefs.description: Maps a short local name (used by slots) to a lexicon id to load, e.g. { "given": "elven-given" }. The indirection lets a pack swap or share lexicons without editing every slot.

config.description: Strategy-specific payload. Shape depends on 'strategy' (see allOf below for 'template').

corpus.description: Key into the pack's lexiconRefs map, pointing at a training-word lexicon (a plain list of example names, not raw text).

order.description: N-gram context length in characters. Higher orders track corpus style more closely but generalize less.

minLength.description: Shortest name (in characters) to accept before retrying the walk.

maxLength.description: Longest name (in characters) before the walk is cut off.

slots.description: Keyed by slot name; referenced from format patterns as {slotName} and from derivations as 'produces'/'source'.

derivations.description: Rules that compute a slot's value from a parent result's part instead of sampling a lexicon. Used for patronymics, clan-prefix surnames, generational suffixes, etc. Only relevant when generate() is called with a parent/kin context.

lexicon.description: Key into the pack's lexiconRefs map.

variants.description: Variant keys this slot accepts, e.g. ['masc','fem','neutral']. Open vocabulary — packs may define their own beyond the common three.

shareWithin.description: When generating multiple results in the same group context (e.g. 'kin'), later calls inherit this slot's value from the first result in the group instead of re-rolling.

optional.description: If true, formats may list this slot in 'requires' and it's valid for it to be absent.

pattern.description: Token pattern for generated (non-lexicon) values, e.g. serials or callsigns. Tokens: {L}/{l} random upper/lowercase letter, {D} random digit 0-9. Any other character passes through literally.

derivedSlot.description: This slot is never sampled directly. It resolves only when a derivation with matching 'produces' fires against a parent context; otherwise it is absent. At least one derivation in this pack's config.derivations should target it (enforced by the pack loader, not this schema).

weight.description: Relative selection weight among this pack's eligible formats.

pattern.description: Template combining slot tokens and literal text, e.g. '{given} {family} of Clan {clan}'.

requires.description: Slot names that must have resolved to a non-empty value for this format to be eligible. Use for formats built around optional or derived slots.

produces.description: Name of the slot in this pack's config.slots that this rule can fill.

source.description: Name of the slot on the parent result to read the base value from (looked up in parent.parts).

weight.description: Relative chance this derivation fires instead of a competing derivation for the same target slot, when a parent context is present.

pattern.description: Regex (no flags) applied to the source value before templating.

variants.description: Maps a requested variant key (or '*' as fallback) to a template string. {source} is replaced with the (optionally stripped) parent value, e.g. { "masc": "{source}ovich", "fem": "{source}ovna" }.
